notes:
Better controller bug reports, especially for wireless pairing problems.

Nothing about how your console plays changes in this update.

If a controller works while it is attached to the rails but will not connect wirelessly,
that used to be very hard to diagnose. Linux cannot pair a Switch controller itself, it
can only copy the pairing your Switch already made, and the file that carries the
pairing across is deleted once it has been used. So afterwards nothing could tell
whether a controller's pairing had ever reached Linux at all.

The console now keeps a small permanent record of that: for each controller, when its
pairing was last seen on the Switch side and when it was last saved on the Linux side.
Your controller report includes that record, your saved pairings by name and address,
and the Bluetooth log that says whether a controller was refused when it tried to
connect. Pairing keys themselves are never included.

The controller report also now says which version you are on and what PPSSPP and DraStic
did with your controller. You will find it under Debug in the file manager page. It is
long, so save it as a file and attach it rather than pasting it.

The pairing record is a system component, so it starts recording one restart after this
update installs.
